blocks.title: Why we work this way
blocks.body:
Most businesses end up with one company for the website, another for the app, a freelancer for ads and a separate vendor for billing software. Things get lost between them.

We put those jobs under one roof. The people who design your screens sit next to the people who build them and the people who bring customers to them.

posts.title: How to brief a web team in ten minutes
posts.intro: A short, clear brief saves weeks. You do not need a long document, only honest answers to four questions.

body.heading: Who is it for?
body.text: Describe one real customer: what they do, what they are looking for, and what device they are probably holding. A site built for everyone works for no one.

body.heading: What should they do?
body.text: Pick one main action. Call you, book a slot, buy a product, or fill in a form. Every page should make that one action easy.

body.heading: What do you already have?
body.text: List your logo, photos, text, domain and any old site. Knowing what exists tells the team what must be made from scratch.

body.heading: How will you know it worked?
body.text: Choose a number you can check in three months: enquiries per week, orders per day, or calls from the site. That number guides every decision after launch.

posts.title: When a spreadsheet stops being enough
posts.intro: Most businesses start by tracking customers in a spreadsheet, and that is fine. These are the signs it is time for a CRM.

body.heading: Leads are slipping
body.text: If someone enquired last week and nobody followed up, the sheet is not reminding anyone. A CRM does.

body.heading: Two people edit the same row
body.text: Once more than one person handles customers, you need to see who spoke to whom and when, without asking around.

body.heading: You cannot answer simple questions
body.text: How many enquiries came in this month? Where did they come from? How many became sales? If that takes an afternoon to work out, you have outgrown the sheet.

body.heading: Start small
body.text: A CRM does not need fifty fields. Begin with name, need, next step and date. Add more only when someone asks for it twice.

posts.title: What to automate first in a small business
posts.intro: Automation pays off fastest on jobs that are frequent, boring and follow the same steps every time.

body.heading: Answering the same questions
body.text: Opening hours, prices, delivery areas. A chatbot on your site or WhatsApp can answer these at any hour and hand over to a person when it gets stuck.

body.heading: Following up
body.text: A message the day after an enquiry, a reminder before an appointment, a thank-you after a purchase. These are easy to automate and easy to forget by hand.

body.heading: Moving data between tools
body.text: If someone copies orders from a form into a sheet and then into billing, that is three chances for a typo. Connect the tools once and the copying stops.

body.heading: Keep a person in the loop
body.text: Automate the routine, not the judgement. Complaints, refunds and unusual requests should still reach a human quickly.
